title: The role of emotions in the construction and dissemination of disinformation on Twitter. A comparison between Brazil and Spain (El papel de las emociones en la construccion y difusion de la desinformacion en Twitter. Una comparativa entre Brasil y Espana)
screen_reason: Spanish-language content analysis of the 100 most-retweeted original tweets of Santiago Abascal (VOX, Spain) and the 99 most-retweeted of Jair Bolsonaro (Brazil), 30 Nov 2020 - 30 Nov 2021, each coded against Wardle & Derakhshan's seven-category mis/disinformation typology. The paper states the number of tweets carrying at least one category (Abascal 77; Bolsonaro 45) against known denominators (100 and 99), i.e. CONTENT shares with explicit denominators.

estimates.country: Espana / Spain (tweets of Santiago Abascal, leader of VOX)
estimates.measure_type: % of a politician's most-retweeted tweets that contain at least one category of mis- or disinformation
estimates.value_raw: 77 tuits que tenian alguna categoria de mis o disinformation, out of 100 tweets (Table 3: 'Don't have' = 23) [EN: 77 tweets that had some category of mis- or disinformation, out of 100]
estimates.denominator: the 100 most-retweeted original tweets posted by @Santi_ABASCAL between 30 Nov 2020 and 30 Nov 2021 (drawn from 338 original tweets in that year)
estimates.definition: A tweet counted if the coders assigned it at least one of Wardle & Derakhshan's (2017) seven mis/disinformation categories - satire or parody, misleading content, imposter content, fabricated content, false connection, false context, manipulated content - after consulting major news media and fact-checking agencies to identify false information; a tweet could receive up to two categories
estimates.misinfo_def: 'Esta ultima [disinformation] es la informacion falsa creada para danar a una persona, una organizacion o un grupo social. Sin embargo, la misinfomation contiene una informacion falsa, pero que no fue creada con una intencion de danar (Wardle y Derakhshan, 2017)' [EN: 'Disinformation is false information created to harm a person, an organisation or a social group. Misinformation, however, contains false information but was not created with an intention to harm']

estimates.page_loc: Section 3.1, pp. 887-888; Table 3 (Clasificacion de mis o disinformation)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two researchers (one Brazilian, one Spanish, each familiar with their country's political context) coded every tweet independently and then discussed; residual doubts were referred to researchers of the Brazilian 'Observatorio de Conflitos' and Spanish 'Disflows' projects; falsity was checked by consulting major news media and fact-checking agencies. A reliability test comparing the two coders is described but NO kappa, ICC or agreement statistic is reported

estimates.notes: JUDGEMENT CALL for the adjudicator on denom_selection: the denominator is BOTH one account's own output (single_source) AND rank-truncated to the 100 most-retweeted tweets out of 338. I coded single_source because the account defines the frame, but the top-N truncation is the more consequential bias and almost certainly inflates the share (the paper's own §3.2 shows mis/disinformation concentrates in high-arousal negative-emotion tweets, which are also the most retweeted). If the codebook prefers the truncation, this is denom_selection=curated. Category counts in Table 3 sum to more than the sample (117 for Abascal) because a tweet could receive up to two categories - the 77 is the count of tweets with at least one, taken from the 'Don't have' row (100 - 23) and stated verbatim in the text.

Same denom_selection judgement call as the Abascal row: one account (single_source) that is also rank-truncated to the most-retweeted 100 of 1,045 tweets, which likely inflates the share.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Emotion-by-misinformation breakdowns were NOT made into rows (they are subgroup splits of the two main rows, by the coders' own emotion coding rather than an audience characteristic): Abascal - 'la muestra espanola esta compuesta por 80 tuits con emociones negativas en las que 66 tienen alguna categoria de mis o disinformation. Esto corresponde a un 82,5%... En cuanto a las emociones positivas, solo 7 de los 18 tuits (37,88%), contenian alguna categoria de mis o disinformation' [EN: 'the Spanish sample comprises 80 tweets with negative emotions, of which 66 have some category of mis- or disinformation, i.e. 82.5%... As for positive emotions, only 7 of the 18 tweets (37.88%) contained any category']. NOTE an internal inconsistency: 7/18 = 38.9%, not 37.88%. Bolsonaro - 'De los 49 posts con emociones negativas, 34 contenian mis o disinformation (un 69,5%); mientras que de los 48 con emociones positivas, solo 12 tenian mis o disinformation (un 25%)' [EN: 'Of the 49 posts with negative emotions, 34 contained mis- or disinformation (69.5%); while of the 48 with positive emotions, only 12 had mis- or disinformation (25%)']. (2) Per-category counts in Table 3 (e.g. Abascal misleading content 49, manipulated content 25; Bolsonaro misleading content 18, false connection 12) were not turned into definition-variant rows because tweets could carry up to two categories, so the categories do not partition the sample and no clean stricter-definition share (e.g. 'fabricated only') is derivable without a cross-category sum (R8). (3) Emotion distributions (Abascal: anger 71, disgust 33, pleasant 18; Bolsonaro: pleasant 48, disgust 32, anger 25) are not misinformation measures. (4) Figures cited from other work in the introduction (disinformation 70% more likely to go viral; 64% of Brazilians and 53% of Spaniards get news via social media, Newman et al. 2022) come from elsewhere and are barred by R8. (5) The qualitative walk-through of the five most-retweeted tweets per politician gives per-tweet verdicts, not additional shares.

rob.design: Comparative content analysis of two purposively selected far-right politicians' Twitter accounts. All original tweets over one year (30 Nov 2020 - 30 Nov 2021) were collected via the Twitter API using scripts from the 'Observatorio de Conflitos' (Brazil) and 'Disflows' (Spain) projects: 1,383 tweets in total (338 Abascal, 1,045 Bolsonaro). Analysis was restricted to the 100 most-retweeted tweets of each account (99 for Bolsonaro after one deletion) - a rank truncation the authors justify as capturing the posts with most reach. Two coders (one per country) coded emotions (Ekman's primary emotions) and mis/disinformation (Wardle & Derakhshan's seven-category typology) independently, then reconciled by discussion, with unresolved cases referred to the wider project teams; falsity was verified by consulting major media and fact-checking agencies. A 'reliability test' is claimed but NO agreement statistic is reported. Tweets could receive up to two categories per variable. Small samples (100 and 99), single-platform, two individuals only - not generalisable beyond these two accounts, and the top-N-by-retweets selection is not representative of either politician's full output.
rob.item6_quote: La segunda variable utilizada tiene como fundamentacion teorica los estudios de Wardle y Derakhshan (2017) sobre mis y disinformation, donde su conceptualizacion sobre las information disorder llega a una tipologia de siete categorias de mis y disinformation (Tabla 2). En este caso, el analisis de contenido sobre desinformacion se complemento con una consulta de los principales medios de comunicacion y de las agencias de verificacion de datos para identificar algun tipo de informacion falsa. [EN: 'The second variable is theoretically grounded in Wardle & Derakhshan's (2017) work on mis- and disinformation, whose conceptualisation of information disorder yields a typology of seven categories (Table 2). Here the content analysis of disinformation was complemented by consulting the main news media and fact-checking agencies in order to identify any type of false information.']
rob.item10_quote: los resultados indican que 54 de los tuits publicados por Bolsonaro no contienen ninguna categoria de mis o disinformation, mientras que en las publicaciones de Abascal ese numero se reduce a 23. [EN: 'the results indicate that 54 of the tweets published by Bolsonaro contain no category of mis- or disinformation, whereas for Abascal's posts that number falls to 23.']
